clue.text: Wear another hat — it's not his first ball

definitions.meaning: to put on a different hat, specifically swapping one's bowler hat for another
in cricket a ... is one brought on after the opening bowlers, so he does not bowl the first ball of the innings

explanation.surface: Someone swaps headgear, and a remark follows about whose ball it was first.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOWLER is a round felt hat; in cricket a 'change bowler' comes on to relieve the opening pair, who bowl the first balls of an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings are idioms: swapping a felt hat, and the cricket term for a relief bowler.

clue.text: Canons in opposition retaining new authority

parts.note: a cathedral chapter is the body of canons

indicators.note: retaining means one word holds another inside it, here the word for opposition holding new

parts.note: adverse means hostile or in opposition

explanation.surface: Churchmen who disagree nonetheless keep hold of a fresh authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' puts N into ADVERSE after its A, giving ANDVERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Citing chapter and verse means giving the precise source, an idiom for authoritative backing.

clue.text: Reserved for a rising jester

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a fool is a court jester

explanation.surface: Something is set aside for a jester who is getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns FOOL to LOOF, written upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person keeps their distance, a close synonym of standoffish.

clue.text: Good French for the love of allure

parts.note: l'amour is French for 'the love'

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's good word for the love of charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is attractive charm, a near synonym of allure.

clue.text: Little creature first to go through big needle

indicators.note: going through means one piece is threaded inside the needle word

parts.note: a bodkin is a large blunt needle for threading tape
I is the Roman numeral one, hence first

explanation.surface: A tiny animal is the first to pass through the eye of a large needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go through' puts I inside BODKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodikin is an archaic diminutive meaning a little body, so a small being.

clue.text: Tiny little advertisement Sky used five times

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny

indicators.note: used, in the sense of worked over, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ad is a short advertisement

explanation.surface: A broadcaster runs a small advert five times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is the anagram signal, as in worked over. Sky is the British satellite broadcaster, and 'five times' defines the Monday-to-Friday days.
explanation.definitionFit: Monday to Friday are the working days, five occasions in each week.

clue.text: Revive many internationals, else will damage what needs protection

indicators.note: damage means the letters of these words are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Bringing back lots of overseas matches will harm something fragile.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a designated area is a protected rural zone of conservation value in British planning.

clue.text: From the microscopic … then to the ordinarily small, to be completely with it.

definitions.text: From the microscopic … then to the ordinarily small, to be completely with it.

parts.words: From the microscopic … then to the ordinarily small, to be completely with it.
parts.note: the word for microscopic is spelt the same as the sixty-second unit, so one climbs from one sense to the other, and the phrase means fully current

explanation.surface: Scaling up from the tiny to the merely small, one becomes fully fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: MINUTE pronounced my-NEWT is microscopic; pronounced MIN-it it is a small unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for completely current or modern.

clue.text: See 6
Good girl, not the last of singing sisters, on a roll with notes

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

indicators.note: this tells us to drop the final letter of the word for one of the sisters

parts.note: the Nolans were a British singing sister group, so a girl among them is a Nolan

explanation.surface: A well-behaved girl, though not the youngest of a singing family, rolls along with music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl' with 'singing sisters' means one of the Nolans, a 1970s-80s British girl group; 'not the last of' cuts A NOLAN to ANOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a player piano that plays music punched as holes on a paper roll.

clue.text: See 13

parts.note: the French phrase in the cross-referenced starter literally means outside the work

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is the French expression from 13 and 10 translated literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Translating the French word by word gives the English idiom for unemployed.

clue.text: Board game can be played back

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a Strad, a Stradivarius violin, is something that can be played

explanation.surface: A board game that can be replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing arrows at a board.

clue.text: Starter but one that doesn't get to the finish, awfully overdue

indicators.text: that doesn't get to the finish
indicators.note: the horse word fails to reach its own last letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: the 'one' in a race is a horse

indicators.note: awfully signals the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A racehorse that fails to finish is terribly late.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter is the first course of a meal, also called an appetiser.

clue.text: Old female bird's attempt at reef

parts.note: granny is an informal word for an old woman
the knot is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A grandmother's bird tries to reach the reef.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny knot is the common failed version of the reef knot.
explanation.definitionFit: This knot results when one tries a reef knot but crosses the ends the wrong way.

clue.text: Border in which support is for case of Old Testament speak

indicators.note: in which means the border word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a hem is the border of a cloth
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A hem holds a support for an instance of biblical language.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebraism is an idiom or expression characteristic of Hebrew, the language of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Found by locator, men one of whom broke the bank

definitions.text: one of whom broke the bank

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and recast it, so these letters are recast into a new shape

explanation.surface: A gambler, discovered by a tracker of men, ruined the casino.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song 'The Man Who Broke the Bank at Monte Carlo' gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monaco casino resort is famous from the song about a gambler breaking its bank.

clue.text: Waugh's king with gold for starter

indicators.note: gold replaces the first letter, the starter, of the king's name

parts.note: Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Waugh's monarch had gold as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Auberon Waugh was the journalist son of the novelist Evelyn Waugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Auberon was the first name of the writer Waugh, son of Evelyn.

clue.text: Walker to cape in Italy

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with
Cape Horn, so horn can stand for a cape

explanation.surface: A hiker heads for a headland in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leghorn is the old English name for Livorno, a port city in Italy.

clue.text: Fuel said to be in 10

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken aloud, here the French word in 10

parts.note: the light 10 holds the French d'oeuvre

explanation.surface: A fuel that apparently appears in entry 10.
explanation.walkthrough: D'oeuvre is pronounced like DERV, British diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is diesel fuel for road vehicles in British usage.

clue.text: Half the HP in Arthur's queen

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the queen's name, so the surrounding ones go

parts.note: Guinevere was the wife of King Arthur

explanation.surface: Half the hire purchase is owed by Arthur's queen.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is hire purchase, colloquially 'the never-never' in Britain, so half of it is NEVER, found within GUINEVERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire purchase is nicknamed the never-never, so half that slang phrase gives this word.

clue.text: Old shooter's position in crime that's my loss

indicators.note: in means the berth word sits inside the other
the crime word loses the letters of my

parts.note: bigamy is the crime of marrying while already married
a berth is a position or job

explanation.surface: A veteran gunman's role in a crime he regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's my loss' deletes MY from the crime, leaving BIGA, and 'in' places the position inside that remnant. The surface's 'shooter' is a gun, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Bertha was a huge German howitzer of the First World War, an old gun.

clue.text: Provide at last half what's due

parts.note: at last means in the end

indicators.note: half means only the first two of four letters are kept

parts.note: what is due is owed

explanation.surface: Finally hand over half of a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to provide funds or qualities to someone.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: about means the row word goes round the other

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: An argument about a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but is a line, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of small dog.

clue.text: Former boat racer's topping yellow colour

indicators.note: topping means cutting off the top letter

parts.note: gold is a yellow colour
blue is a colour

explanation.surface: An ex-rower's favourite shade is yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is someone who rowed for Oxford or Cambridge in the Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Blue is a former university sportsman, here an Oxford or Cambridge rower.

clue.text: Fixed method for training

parts.note: permanent means fixed
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A settled approach to coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' reads as coaching but means running trains on.
explanation.definitionFit: The permanent way is the railway track, the line trains run along.
